label: D2 arriving at S1 in the first two trials of an episode
explanation: Fires only at D2, only when the state input is S1, and only at the very start of an episode (ep_trial 0-1; there is a weak tail at trials 2-9). It never fires at D1 or GO, on S2, or after trial 9. Magnitude is set mainly by episode position. On trial 0 it is near max (all of the top quartile; ~86% of the mass), and in practice that is almost always a2 then a rare transition to S1, because the untrained-prior first choice is nearly always a2. On trial 1 it is weak (~0.04-0.1 of max). On trial 1 it is silent when the previous reward was 1: adding prev_reward == 0 gives precision 1.0 but lowers recall (dev F1 0.84 vs 0.86), so the simpler predicate was recorded. All variables used are observed at D2 (state is shown and ep_trial is position), so uses_future is false. It is best read as a reached-S1 detector at episode onset, active before the hidden state has built up.

issues: The core claims hold on dev. Every activation is at D2 (D1 and GO: 0 of 590 active). There are no activations on S2 at D2 and none at ep_trial > 9. ep_trial==0 & D2 & S1 has precision 1.0 and holds 86% of the activation mass (test: 87%). The 8 trial-0 a1-to-S1 common cases also all fire, so the trial-0 response is to the S1 arrival itself, not to the rare transition.

The explanation says the feature is 'silent when the previous reward was 1' at trial 1. That is false. With ep_trial==1 & D2 & S1 & prev_reward==1, precision is 0.478, so about half of those steps fire. With tv('reward',-1)==1, precision is 0.489 on dev and 0.480 on test.

The real rule at trial 1 is narrower. The feature is silent only when trial 0 reached S1 and was rewarded: tv('state',-1)==S1 & tv('reward',-1)==1 gives precision 0.0 (71 steps). It fires in every other trial-1 case: previous trial rewarded at S2 gives precision 1.0 (68 steps); previous trial unrewarded gives precision 1.0 whether the previous state was S1 (26) or S2 (116). In the silent case the agent usually repeats a1 and lands on S1 by a common transition; 71 of the 72 a1 cases are silent.

This silent case is a systematic false-positive class: about 71 of the predicate's 119 false positives on dev. The original predicate's trial-1 component has precision of only 0.75 on dev and 0.77 on test.

The weak tail at ep_trial 2-9 is real but small: about 10% of active steps and 2% of the mass. It is scattered, with precision of about 0.015 even when restricted to a2 choices, so it is acceptable noise.
None of the variables used is a future variable (state at D2, ep_trial, and the previous trial's state and reward are all observed).
